Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old male presents with 3 days of diarrhea, central abdominal pain, and one episode of vomiting. No evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding; likely acute gastroenteritis; advised supportive management and red flag monitoring.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute Gastroenteritis
- 3 days of diarrhea, central abdominal pain (under the belly button), and one episode of vomiting.
- Pain described as central, does not radiate, slightly relieved after passing stool; some associated abdominal sounds.
- No blood in stool or vomit.
- One episode of vomiting after eating fruit; currently able to tolerate some oral intake but limiting intake due to ongoing symptoms.
- No reported fever; patient reports some sweating last four days but denies clear febrile episodes.
- No chest pain, no worsening of baseline asthma/breathing status.
- No recent consumption of suspect food recalled; unsure of possible food triggers.
- Symptoms have neither improved nor worsened over three days.
- Physical findings: Tenderness upon self-palpation of abdomen.
- No red flags identified during consult (no blood, significant pain escalation, or severe systemic features).
- Impression: Likely acute infectious gastroenteritis.

Issue 2: Asthma
- History of asthma; uses inhaler (type/brand and dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No current worsening of breathing, chest pain, or functional limitation beyond baseline.
- New inhaler (brand unspecified) recently obtained.
- Doubts about inhaler being trigger for current GI symptoms (clinician advised unlikely).

Issue 3: Family History of Bowel Cancer
- Father died of bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.
- Patient expresses concern regarding personal risk for bowel malignancy.
- No features suggestive of bowel malignancy at this time (no blood in stool, short symptom duration).

Medications:
- Inhaler for asthma (brand/type/dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- NKDA (No Known Drug Allergies).

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.

Social History:
- Unable to attend work due to frequent need for toilet access.
- Smoking history, alcohol intake, and living arrangements not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No details provided regarding cervical screening test, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, vaccination history, optometry review, or recent skin check.

Physical Examination:
- Self-reported abdominal tenderness to palpation.
- No measured vitals documented.
- No in-person physical examination performed.

Plan:
- Advise increased oral fluid intake to prevent dehydration.
- Monitor for red flags: onset of fever, blood in stool or vomitus, escalating abdominal pain, or inability to tolerate oral intake.
- Stay home from work until improvement noted.
- No antibiotics prescribed (advised likely self-limiting viral infection).
- If symptoms worsen or do not improve in 1-2 days, or concerning signs develop, arrange in-person GP review for further assessment.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):

●	Missing: Medication details (full name, dose, route, frequency); allergies and asthma history documented but no reconciliation of full medication list; smoking/alcohol history not obtained.
●	No internal transcript conflicts identified.
●	Transcript overall clear, clinically relevant details extracted; some minor conversational noise but did not impact extraction of clinical detail.
